items.summary: Analyzes 5.5 years of Foursquare check-in data for about 10,000 venues in London and Barcelona, identifying six recurring popularity trajectory shapes including Rise, Fall, Ephemeral, and Underdogs. Challenges the assumption that venue fortunes simply track neighborhood wealth and population, linking trajectory types to mixing patterns. A computational social science study with urban-planning implications.

items.title: Instruction-Conditioned Motion Control for Robotic Arms: Language-to-Code Decomposition and Reinforcement Learning
items.content: arXiv:2610.19617v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Instruction-Conditioned Motion Control (ICMC) separates parameter specification, instruction generation, and code synthesis for language-driven robot control, making execution outcomes traceable to instructions and programs. We compare one-shot generation with ICMC under o1 and o4-mini on cube pick-and-place and letter-reshaping tasks for a UR5e arm in MuJoCo. We then train an open-weight instruction policy by GRPO through a frozen code generator on cube placement onto two- and five-cube letter layouts, averaging the rewards of five programs per instruction. The logged positive-reward rate rose from 31.6% to 35.3% (253/800 to 282/800) between the first and last five training steps. A log audit identifies positive binary labels associated with geometric-failure messages: at least 19 in that run, 18 in the dense-reward run, and 5 in the run with one program per instruction. In one case, all five rewards were 1.0 while the log reports a 0.9515 m miss against a 0.05 m tolerance; the verdict came from the program's own output stream. We distinguish logged reward rates from independently verified task success and report descriptive results for each configuration's single training trajectory. We introduce an independent evaluation protocol that checks task completion against fixed specifications, separating robot control from success assessment to support reproducible evaluation.

items.summary: ICMC separates parameter specification, instruction generation, and code synthesis for language-driven robot control, making execution outcomes traceable to instructions and programs. The authors compare one-shot generation with ICMC using o1 and o4-mini on UR5e manipulation in MuJoCo and train an instruction policy via GRPO, reporting a modest rise in positive-reward rate from 31.6% to 35.3%.
items.reasoning: The interpretability-oriented decomposition of language-to-code control is interesting, but the empirical gains are small, the task scope is limited to synthetic cube manipulation, and reliance on o1/o4-mini outputs raises questions about generalization; it reads more like an exploratory study.

items.title: PPA 5: Improper Priors and the Infinite SIA
items.content:
[This is the fifth piece in my series on the Parametric Process Assumption (PPA), a new model of anthropics. You should start here if you are just seeing this for the first time.

The previous piece is "Parametric Modeling and Types of Uncertainty."

TLDR:

- Improper priors allow you to use a prior that is not a true distribution. They can be updated and, with enough new information, be made proper Until there is enough information to become proper, improper priors cannot be used to make predictions
- The SIA over universes with potentially infinite observers can be thought of as an improper prior that updates to proper once you learn enough about your identity

The next piece is "Indexical Models Don't Have Diversity Biases."]

## Not all priors make predictions

[If you already know what an improper prior is and why the SIA functions as one, then you may wish to skip to the "SIA as an improper prior” section]

One thing that everyone knows is that it is not possible to make a uniform selection over the set of all integers. If you tried to make a uniform distribution over this range, you would have to assign each number a probability of 1/, which is just equal to zero, and adding up an infinite number of zeros just gets you zero, not 1.[1]

I have seen this fact used to argue that, since identities are selected uniformly, neither the SIA nor the SSA can actually construct a probability distribution over infinite observers. At minimum, I myself have erroneously made claims of this sort in the past.

In reality, however, there are many different ways that the distribution of observers can be infinite, and at least a couple of tricks we can do to get valid results.[2] The more technical parts of this series will go through a whole bunch of these. For now, what I want to talk about is the concept of an improper prior⁠....

items.summary: Explains how improper priors (priors that are not true probability distributions) can still be updated and become proper with sufficient evidence, and reframes the SIA over infinite-observer universes as such an improper prior. This offers a principled way to handle anthropics in infinite cosmologies.
items.reasoning: Connects a real statistical concept (improper priors) to anthropic paradoxes in a mathematically literate way, addressing a genuine known problem (SIA with infinities), though the audience and impact remain niche.

items.title: A Hybrid Kinematic GCN and Elastic Transformer for Efficient Indian Sign Language Recognition
items.content: arXiv:2610.14680v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Sign Language Recognition (SLR) presents complex challenges due to variable signing speeds and spatial intricacies. Specifically, Indian Sign Language (ISL) requires precise modeling of its inherently bimanual nature and is bottlenecked by the scarcity of large-vocabulary benchmarks and the inability of standard models to handle irregular signing velocities. To address this, a structurally-aware hybrid framework for efficient, gloss ISL recognition is proposed. To minimize computational redundancy, an entropy-driven SVD sampler that dynamically extracts informative keyframes is used. Because this subsampling creates irregular physical time gaps, the proposed architecture employs a Continuous Dual Positional Encoding paired with a distance-aware Elastic Transformer to preserve natural signing rhythm. Spatially, a Kinematically-Conditioned Adaptive GCN explicitly models bimanual geometry using unified bone-joint features. To validate our framework, a 120-class, 9,453-video native ISL dataset is created. Augmented by Physical Node Dropout and ArcFace optimization to mitigate subject-specific memorization, our framework achieves a competitive 89.8% accuracy, establishing a strong baseline for complex sign language modeling.

items.reasoning: A competent application paper addressing a genuine accessibility need and the under-served ISL domain with thoughtful architectural handling of irregular dynamics. However, it is an applied architecture combination rather than an advance likely to influence the broader field.

items.title: Single-Sample Decoding of a Two-Layer Sound-Word Canvas Model for Thai Klon Pad
items.content: arXiv:2610.14980v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We present a generator of Thai klon pad verse, one stanza from a short topic, and evaluate it against human verse on held-out topics. The generator is a masked language model initialised from WangchanBERTa over a fixed canvas with two layers: a sound layer of pronounced syllables, where rhyme, tone and syllable count are enforced as hard masks, and a word layer of whole words, so that no word is cut into written pieces. Decoding commits one cell at a time and samples at temperature 0.4; one sample is drawn per topic, with no selection, reranking or repair. On 78 held-out topics never used in development, judged by three independent runs of a frozen LLM judge in the same pools as the human stanzas from which the topics were written, 70.5% of the generated stanzas pass form, lexical cleanness of all four lines and topic alignment together, against 76.9% for the human stanzas (difference -6.4 points, 95% CI [-19.2, +6.4]). Cleanness is level with human (85.9% vs. 87.2%), and the stanzas pass form and cleanness together slightly more often than the human ones (+3.8 points, [-6.4, +14.1]); the difference lies in alignment (84.6% vs. 91.0%), on topics that were written from the human stanzas. The low temperature matters: at higher temperatures the same model passes clearly fewer of the same topics, because lexical errors lie in the model's lower-probability choices; sharpening the sampling distribution removes most of them, at a cost in vocabulary (7.5% rare words against 16.5% in the human stanzas) and diversity. The pre-registered target, all-three within 5 points of human, is missed by 1.4 points. KlonSuphap-LM, the only public klon pad generator we know of, passes none of the 78 held-out topics when judged in separate pools together with the method's and the human stanzas (form 19.2%, cleanness 3.8%).
items.author: Worasait Suwannik
items.summary: Presents a generator for traditional Thai klon pad verse using a masked language model (initialized from WangchanBERTa) over a two-layer canvas enforcing rhyme, tone, and syllable constraints as hard masks. With single-sample decoding and no reranking, 70.5% of generations on held-out topics are judged comparable to human stanzas.
items.reasoning: A well-executed niche contribution: the constrained canvas approach with hard phonological masks and no-selection decoding is technically clean, and evaluation against human verse on held-out topics is rigorous for this scale. However, domain specificity (Thai poetry) limits broader impact.

KlonSuphap-LM, the only public klon pad generator we know of, passes none of the 78 held-out topics when judged in separate pools together with the method's and the human stanzas (form 19.2%, cleanness 3.8%).

items.title: Analyzing the Dynamics of WSBM-based Echo State Networks using InputDSA
items.content: arXiv:2610.15380v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Bridging the structural gap between biological brains and artificial neural networks presents a pathway to altered computational dynamics. This paper introduces a Reservoir Computing framework that replaces random networks with biologically realistic modularity by applying the Weighted Stochastic Block Model (WSBM) to Echo State Networks (ESNs). This topological parameterization constructs reservoirs reflecting latent functional sub-circuits. Furthermore, the integration of Input Dynamical Similarity Analysis (InputDSA) provides a mechanism to isolate and compare how structural priors modulate intrinsic recurrent dynamics versus external inputs. By evaluating these architectures, we establish that structural diversity does not necessarily predicts behavioral diversity across the selected network subset. Furthermore, our demixed analysis confirms Anna Karenina principle of dynamics, demonstrating that environmental constraints enforce dynamical convergence in successful agents, while failing networks degenerate into idiosyncratic trajectories.
items.author: Huy Mai, Robert Clarke
items.summary: This work introduces a reservoir computing framework that replaces random Echo State Network reservoirs with biologically realistic modular structure via the Weighted Stochastic Block Model, and pairs it with Input Dynamical Similarity Analysis to separate the effects of structural priors from external input signals on recurrent dynamics. The findings indicate structural diversity alone does not automatically confer computational benefits. It contributes to the effort to bridge the gap between biological neural circuits and artificial networks.
items.reasoning: A methodologically careful but niche contribution. Reservoir computing and WSBM-based topology analysis are interesting, and the InputDSA diagnostic is a useful analytical tool, but ESNs are not central to modern deep learning practice and the impact outside this subfield appears limited. Early-career-style authorship and a modest scope keep the score in the middle-low range.

items.title: Data Portability Revisited: Toward the Human-Centric, AI-Driven Data Ecosystems of Tomorrow
items.content: arXiv:2610.15503v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This Article critically examines the contemporary regulatory framework and discourse surrounding data portability in the United States. Using recent regulatory developments in the European Union as an illustration, this Article suggests that although data access and portability are identified as vital issues in multiple policy instruments, in its current iteration, at least, legal conceptions of portability continue to reinforce the interests of service providers and data controller enterprises rather than individual end users. This Article argues that a paradigm shift toward a more human-centric data approach to data governance must occur, under which data would be recognized as fundamental to an individual's identity in a digital age. Therefore, it should be placed in the hands of individuals rather than service providers or data controller enterprises. This Article considers technical and market trends in the European Union that reveal and facilitate such a change. It suggests that regulatory frameworks should better align with these technological and market developments to encourage change-inducing trends among market actors. In short, this Article identifies a transformative approach to data portability that empowers individuals with the freedom and ability to aggregate their data in secure personal spaces under their control or dominion. Such a human-centric perspective on data portability is crucial in building Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered applications for individual consumers that can pave the way for the human-centric, AI-driven data ecosystems of the future.

items.title: Vision: "What Don't I Know About User's Preferences?" How Uncertainty Estimation Improves Proactive Assistant Alignment
items.content: arXiv:2610.15948v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Proactive Smart Assistants (PSAs) increasingly use general knowledge, learned patterns from group-level data, patterns from individual user's data, and recent sensor observations to anticipate which action a user may prefer. Existing systems typically select actions from predicted user preference likelihoods, but these likelihoods alone do not reveal how reliable the prediction is, which evidence supports it, or why ambiguity remains. In this vision paper, we argue that uncertainty estimation can provide this missing information and substantially change appropriate downstream behavior. Using the example of a home assistant, we introduce the questions that uncertainty estimation aims to answer, i.e. how sure is the assistant about the predicted preference likelihood, whether the confidence come from group-level assumptions or individual's data, and whether likelihood ambiguity reflect the user's intrinsic preference variability or insufficient data for the particular situation. We further introduce uncertainty estimation applications in neighboring domains, such as human trajectory prediction, personalized activity recognition, information-collection, and model-based control. Finally, we draw on insights from neighboring domains to envision how future uncertainty-aware proactive assistants may address key challenges in proactive interaction.
items.author: Zhiyu An, Ziyi Xuan, Yu Yang, Wan Du
items.summary: This vision paper argues that proactive smart assistants should complement preference-likelihood predictions with uncertainty estimation, revealing prediction reliability, supporting evidence, and residual ambiguity. Using a home-assistant example, it outlines the questions uncertainty estimation should answer and how they should change downstream assistant behavior.
items.reasoning: The argument that uncertainty should inform proactive assistant actions is sound but well trodden in the broader uncertainty literature; as a vision paper it offers no empirical results or new methods. Its value is mainly agenda-setting for a specific application area.

items.title: FON: A Draft-Revise Dual-Organ Language Model without Sequence-Level Quadratic Attention
items.content: arXiv:2610.16301v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Self-attention assigns two functions to one mechanism-where to read and how to mix-at the price of O(L^2) training, an O(T) decode state, and position signals bound to the training length. Existing attention-free alternatives all optimize the single function of generation. We propose FON (Fusion-Organ Network), which differentiates one weight stack into a drafting organ (multi-tap learnable delays + content-adaptive recursion; causal, O(S) training, O(1) decode state, no sequence-level quadratic attention) and a revision organ that re-processes the written prefix through multi-scale ripple kernels injected via weak gates, never generating. At 30M parameters, iso-parameter and iso-token budget, FON reaches perplexity 131.03 on WikiText-103, beating Transformer (197.73) and Mamba2 (152.53); the advantage persists under all depth-aligned baselines and at the 70M tier (-20.8%). At 8x length extrapolation FON degrades by ~8-9% without positional-encoding engineering, between ALiBi and RoPE. The revision channel provides a structural pathway for in-domain infilling that causal architectures lack in principle (+19% over on-demand coupling), at a perplexity cost indistinguishable within measurement precision. We report all costs and boundaries: impaired long-range retrieval, synthetic-task disadvantages, weaker out-of-domain code infilling than a same-recipe Transformer, and a 6.5-12.3x wall-clock gap.
items.author: Helong Hu (Zhanjiang Campus, Guangdong Ocean University, Zhanjiang, Guangdong, China), Hongdan Pan (Maoming Administrative Service Center, Maoming, Guangdong, China), Shuiqing Hu (China Pacific Insurance)
items.summary: FON (Fusion-Organ Network) is an attention-free language model that splits computation into a drafting organ with O(1) decode state and a revision organ that reprocesses the prefix via multi-scale kernels. At only 30M parameters it reports perplexity of 131.03 on WikiText-103 under iso-parameter and iso-token budgets.
items.reasoning: Novel architectural direction decoupling reading and mixing to avoid quadratic attention, but results are limited to very small 30M-parameter scale, and the reported perplexity is far from competitive with modern LMs. Author affiliations are non-research institutions, reducing credibility for language-model claims.

items.title: Towards Resilience: Slice-Driven Orchestration of Mobile IoMT in 6G-Edge-Continuum
items.content: arXiv:2610.17296v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Emerging healthcare services, such as real-time diagnostics, remote health monitoring and computer-assisted surgery, require stringent Quality of Service (QoS) guarantees while operating under limited and heterogeneous edge resources. Existing Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) orchestration methods primarily focus on communication metrics such as latency and bandwidth, while overlooking edge resource constraints and dynamic adaptation to workload and user mobility. This paper presents a novel resource-slicing-based adaptive orchestration framework that integrates 5G network slicing (NS), resource-aware orchestration, and mobility-aware task offloading into a single adaptive system. IoMT services are assigned to distinct 5G network slices while jointly considering CPU capacity, memory availability and amount of storage, enabling more efficient service placement and execution. In addition, the system supports user mobility and dynamic task offloading to maintain service continuity under changing network conditions. SimPy-based simulation demonstrates that the proposed method enhances service deployment efficiency, reduces request blocking, and improves user acceptance while maintaining reliable performance across diverse IoMT scenarios.

It targets QoS guarantees for latency-sensitive healthcare applications under constrained and heterogeneous edge resources.

items.title: WisdomNet: trustable machine learning toward error-free classification
items.content: arXiv:2610.15299v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Misclassification is a critical problem in many machine learning applications. Since even the classifier models with high accuracy (e.g., > 95%) still introduce some misclassification error, it may not be possible to rely on the output of a classifier. In this paper, we introduce trustable learning, which prompts the learning model to yield only the true output, thus avoiding misclassifications. Whenever the model cannot decide the output accurately, the learning model should indicate that there could be a misclassification error if it is forced to classify, and hence, it should reject to make a decision or defer it to a human expert. Therefore, we develop a methodology for trustable learning and apply it to artificial neural networks and show that it is possible to develop a classifier with 0% misclassification error. We propose a novel neural network architecture named WisdomNet that could provide zero prediction error by introducing an additional neuron named as conjugate neuron that would indicate whether the network is able to classify the data correctly or not. The WisdomNet architecture can be applied to any previously built model, and we have evaluated WisdomNet with several network architectures such as multilayer perceptron, convolutional neural network, and deep network on different data sets. The results show that the WisdomNet is able to reduce the classification error rate to 0%, while labeling the data is difficult to classify as `reject' at a low percentage of within around 10%.
items.author: Truong X. Tran, Ramazan S. Aygun
items.summary: WisdomNet proposes a trustable-learning methodology in which models output only predictions they believe are true, otherwise abstaining or deferring to a human expert, aiming toward error-free classification. The method is applied to artificial neural networks and targets applications where misclassification is critical. The framing emphasizes selective prediction and rejection as a path to trustworthy deployment.
items.reasoning: The abstention/selective-prediction idea is well established, so the framing as a new direction understates prior work; the abstract suggests limited empirical scale or novel theoretical machinery. Practical value in high-stakes classification settings, but limited novelty relative to the rejection-sampling and learning-to-defer literature.

items.title: Assessing the Performance of AI Models in Misinformation Detection Using Predefined Social Noise Constructs
items.content: arXiv:2610.17469v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Social media platforms generate vast volumes of user-generated content that often obscure meaningful discourse, a phenomenon conceptualized as social noise. While existing misinformation detection methods primarily focus on factual verification, they largely overlook the role of social noise in amplifying misinformation. This study assesses the performance of six text-based models and a graph neural network (GNN) in mitigating the effects of misinformation using predefined social noise constructs. The dataset consists of 500,000 tweets collected from the X platform using the Ukraine hashtag during the Russia-Ukraine conflict from March 2024 to March 2025. Advanced machine learning models achieve strong performance, with accuracies ranging from 79.94% to 97.17%. RoBERTa demonstrates the highest performance, with an accuracy of 97.17%, Cohen's kappa of 0.9660, MCC of 0.9660, and AUC of 0.9977. The GNN achieves an accuracy of 64.52% and an AUC of 0.899, demonstrating performance above random-chance classification by exploiting the relational structure between tweets. All text-based models achieve kappa values greater than 0.75, indicating substantial overall agreement. Explainable AI analysis using LIME reveals that 89.6% of predictive weight is attributed to contextual features rather than isolated keywords. The findings highlight that integrating social noise into AI pipelines enhances misinformation detection and supports more effective mitigation strategies in large-scale social media environments.

items.title: GeoMER: A Joint Euclidean-Hyperbolic Geometry Framework for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
items.content: arXiv:2610.18587v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) aims to understand human emotions by integrating information from multiple modalities such as speech and text. Psychological studies suggest that emotions exhibit latent hierarchical structured relationships in their semantic representations. However, most MER approaches rely on Euclidean representations, which capture fine-grained cross-modal interactions but do not explicitly provide a geometric prior for organizing hierarchical emotional structures. To mitigate this gap, we propose GeoMER, a joint Euclidean-Hyperbolic modeling framework that introduces hyperbolic emotion-core routing to capture higher-level, abstract emotional representations for MER. The proposed framework jointly models token-level cross-modal semantic interactions and latent emotion representations in two complementary geometric spaces. Specifically, GeoMER consists of a Euclidean Multimodal Fusion Module (EuclFusion) for multimodal representation fusion and a Hyperbolic Geometric Core Routing (HypGeoRoute) module that performs geometry-aware core assignment and aggregation in a hyperbolic manifold to capture more abstract feature representations. The HypGeoRoute module complements the Euclidean token-level modeling. We experiment on the IEMOCAP multimodal MER benchmark and demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best performance, with 83.54% weighted accuracy and 83.35% unweighted accuracy, outperforming Euclidean baselines, including MemoCMT.
items.author: Ting Zhu, Huizhi Liang, Boguslaw Obara, Shufei Duan, Varun Ojha
items.summary: GeoMER combines Euclidean and hyperbolic representations for multimodal emotion recognition, using hyperbolic emotion-core routing to capture hierarchical relationships between emotions identified in psychology. It jointly models token-level cross-modal interactions with hierarchical abstract emotional structure. This adds an explicit geometric prior to MER systems.
items.reasoning: Reasonable methodological contribution applying hyperbolic geometry, motivated by psychological structure of emotion. Novelty is moderate since hyperbolic embeddings are well explored; improvements on MER benchmarks would determine significance.

items.title: Integrated Novelty Detection Systems: From Sensor Networks to Multi-Novelty Computer Vision
items.content: arXiv:2610.19347v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Novelty detection is crucial in various technological and scientific domains. Its importance spans from ensuring the reliability of sensor networks to enhancing the adaptability of computer vision systems. As AI systems become increasingly sophisticated and complex, effective anomaly detection is essential for maintaining reliability and accuracy. This work addresses novelty detection in weather sensor networks and computer vision. In weather sensor networks, particularly for monitoring rainfall, detecting blocked rain gauges can significantly impact data reliability, food security, and disaster management. This work evaluates four existing quality control methods for detecting blocked rain gauges and demonstrates their limitations, particularly in detecting clusters of faulty sensors. By comparing methods such as the Conditional Mixture Model (CMM), PSWQ (Fz-filter), Kernel Regression, and Gaussian Method, we identify their shortcomings and propose three novel quality control techniques that integrate probabilistic fault detection and consistency-based diagnosis framework to improve timely detection of blocked sensors, while reducing false alarms.   In the realm of computer vision, current systems often fail to handle multiple types of novelty due to their focus on single-novelty scenarios. We highlight the need for integrated systems capable of handling multiple types of novelty. To support this, we introduce the Novel Snapshot Serengeti (NOVEL-SS) dataset, derived from the Snapshot Serengeti camera trap data, which includes various forms of novelty. We also present the DCA (Detect, Characterize, and Accommodate) baseline system, designed to handle multiple novelty by detecting, characterizing, and accommodating them. This work aims to advance the robustness and adaptability of novelty detection systems across both weather sensor networks and computer vision applications.

items.summary: This thesis-style work addresses novelty detection in two settings: weather sensor networks, where detecting blocked rain gauges matters for data reliability and disaster management, and multi-novelty computer vision. It evaluates four existing quality-control methods for rain gauges, demonstrates their limitations, and extends anomaly-detection ideas toward more capable vision systems.

items.title: Selective Next-Location Prediction with MetaModelSelect: A Lightweight Post-Hoc Confidence Metamodel
items.content: arXiv:2610.19394v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Next-location prediction can support proactive mobile-network decisions, but acting on unreliable predictions can waste resources. We apply MetaModelSelect, a lightweight post-hoc confidence metamodel, to selective cellular next-location prediction. The mobility-specific model combines a learned embedding of the predicted location with the four largest softmax probabilities and Softmax Concentration. It learns whether a frozen recurrent neural network's top-1 prediction is correct, using only its outputs and without retraining the backbone. items.title: Empirical Boundaries of Reservoir Computing for Few-Shot Sequence Pattern Tasks
items.content: arXiv:2610.19997v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Efficient sequence modeling remains a fundamental challenge in machine learning. Despite the success of Transformers, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) have recently re-emerged as efficient alternatives. Particularly, Echo State Networks (ESNs) offer a compelling framework of randomized RNNs that have been extensively studied for time-series forecasting and dynamical systems. This paper presents an empirical analysis of distributional, architectural, and optimization variants of ESNs evaluated on few-shot sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) pattern tasks. These synthetic tasks utilize discrete symbol sequences, characterized by delays, inactive phases, and triggered markers to isolate and evaluate memory and pattern recognition capabilities. The minimality of these tasks is crucial to understand the strengths and limitations of machine learning models. Furthermore, when the input signal utilizes a one-hot encoding, ESN dynamics are governed strictly by their weight distributions, offering an ideal lens through which to study reservoir computing.   Our findings map the performance boundaries of ESNs relative to state-of-the-art (SOTA) models. We show that preserving a linear state regime is vital for memory tasks, such as pattern completion or simple copy. We propose a data-dependent modulation mechanism for nonlinear input injection into the reservoir (G-ESN). G-ESN functions as a statistical filter capable of solving tasks that conventional ESNs cannot (the adding problem and bracket matching). Finally, for Deep ESNs, we evaluate a shared readout mechanism across layers that outperforms conventional concatenated readouts on structural tasks, including selective copy, sorting problem, and bracket matching.

items.title: Selective Growing Q-Networks (SGQN): An Analysis of Adaptive Action Grids in Decoupled Q-Learning
items.content: arXiv:2610.20463v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Value-based Q-learning for continuous control can discretise the action space, but the resolution of the discretisation trades early exploration against final precision. Growing Q-Networks (GQN) grow the resolution uniformly from coarse to fine. We introduce Selective Growing Q-Networks (SGQN), which keeps decoupled Q-learning and replaces uniform growth with an adaptive action grid: bins are added next to bins with high estimated Q-value, bins with low Q-value are pruned, and actions are chosen epsilon-greedily. On eight DeepMind Control Suite (DMControl) tasks with 2 to 12 action dimensions, SGQN has the highest mean final return among the compared methods on four, is within 1.1% of the best method on three more, and is 3.4% below Bang-Bang MPO on Walker Run, using on average 7.5 of 9 available bins per dimension. We then test whether the adaptive grid explains these results, and find that it does not. Growth activates every candidate bin and behaves like uniform growth, and removing pruning changes the return by at most 1.1%. Two other choices matter: starting from a coarse grid, since starting with all 9 bins produces collapsed seeds, and epsilon-greedy selection, since an annealed softmax lowers the return by 23% to 100%. SGQN is insensitive to its growth and pruning hyperparameters. It also differs from the GQN and DecQN baselines in other respects, notably one gradient update per environment step instead of one per eight, which we did not control for, so we do not attribute its advantage to a single component. We present SGQN as a competitive value-based method and as an analysis of which ingredients of a growing action grid matter.

This addresses the exploration-precision tradeoff in action discretization.

items.title: Physics-Guided Multi-Fidelity Surrogate Modeling for Natural Supercavity Geometry of an Axisymmetric Conical Cavitator
items.content: arXiv:2610.18886v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Natural supercavitation behind conical cavitators generates a vapor-filled envelope that, when sustained over the full body of a high-speed underwater vehicles, reduces hydrodynamic skin-friction drag and enables performance levels unattainable in fully wetted flow. Accurate prediction of maximum cavity length and maximum cavity radius and local cavity profile as functions of cavitation number and cone half-angle is essential for both the static design and the real-time shape management of super-cavitating torpedo cavitators. Classical analytical models provide computationally inexpensive predictions but exhibit systematic disagreements in the practically important regime of moderate cavitation number and large angle, where slender-body assumptions begin to break down. Existing data-driven machine learning approaches offer higher accuracy but are constrained by the prohibitive cost of multiphase computational fluid dynamics (CFD) sweeps over the full design space. This study proposes a physics-guided multi-fidelity surrogate framework based on Extended Hierarchical Kriging (PG-EHK) that addresses this challenge by fusing the multiple competing analytical cavity formulas as non-level low-fidelity (LF) trend functions corrected by a sparse set of high-fidelity (HF) CFD data. It simultaneously incorporates the analytical models regardless of their local fidelity ordering, using Bayesian-estimated scaling factors to construct the trend function as physical baseline. The resulting surrogate maps operational condition inputs to cavity geometry responses using fewer than 20 high-fidelity CFD evaluations. Cross-validation on five independent hold-out CFD cases demonstrates that the proposed PG-EHK surrogate achieves 61% reduction in prediction error compared to the best-performing individual analytical approach.

The approach blends cheap classical analytical models with higher-fidelity data in the regime where slender-body assumptions fail. Relevant to design and real-time shape management of super-cavitating underwater vehicles.

items.title: Projected Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao Flows for Hawkes Background-Intensity Estimation
items.content: arXiv:2610.19588v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We consider the problem of estimating the background intensity of a Hawkes process when the triggering mechanism is known, treating the background as an unknown finite positive measure with a regular density. We propose a likelihood-based variational approach based on the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao geometry. In this setting, the relevant first variations are naturally distribution-valued and therefore fall outside the classical gradient-flow formulation. We develop a distributional framework for the resulting dynamics and give them a finite-dimensional meaning through projections onto statistical manifolds. We identify the true background as the unique zero of a limiting generalized gradient and, under suitable stability, compactness, integrability and approximation conditions, establish a conditional consistency theorem for measurable estimators satisfying the empirical projected equations on events whose probabilities tend to one. Finally, we specialize the construction to Gaussian-mixture manifolds and obtain an explicit finite-dimensional scheme.
items.author: Isaias Banales, Arturo Jaramillo
items.summary: The paper proposes a likelihood-based variational method for estimating the background intensity of a Hawkes process using Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao geometry, developing a distributional framework for dynamics whose first variations are distribution-valued. The true background is identified as the unique zero of a limiting generalized gradient, with convergence established under suitable conditions. This is a sophisticated mathematical contribution to point process estimation.

items.title: Twenty Days Later: A Pre-Registered Test of History-Based Forecasts of Brand Mentions in Gemini Answers
items.content: arXiv:2610.19608v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Counts of which brands a large language model names are useful only if they hold long enough to act on. We test this with a pre-registered replication. The same 162 requests (54 questions in English, Estonian and Finnish about three software categories, four of twelve candidate brands per question, three repeats) were sent to gemini-3.1-pro-preview in three waves within about ten hours on 22 and 23 September 2026, and again on 13 October 2026, 20.3 days after the third wave, with identical request bodies. The plan and its decision rule were frozen, hashed and registered on OSF before the first call. The outcome is a lexical mention label per answer and brand, 648 per wave. The primary forecast, each brand-and-question cell's mention rate over the nine earlier answers, scored Brier 0.0281 and log loss 0.126, against Brier 0.0259 for the six-answer forecast of the 8-hour wave and a registered ceiling of 0.0559. It beat brand history (0.104), the overall rate (0.234) and a constant 0.5 (0.250) on both scores and in all nine question families (exact sign-flip p = 0.0039), so durability holds under the registered rule. A forecast frozen from the first wave alone scored 0.0599, 0.0587 and 0.0604 at horizons of 1.5 hours, 9.6 hours and 20.7 days. Of the 202 cells unanimous in the 8-hour wave, 194 were unchanged at D1 and none reversed. The latest wave alone was nearly as accurate as the pooled history (Brier 0.0292; pooled lower in 5 of 9 families, p = 0.28). Every answer reported the requested model version, and none issued a search query although search was enabled. A blind human check of 96 labels agreed with the rule on 94; both disagreements were adjudicated as rater omissions, so after adjudication the rule matched on 96 of 96. The test covers one model, one interval and twelve known brands, and estimates no decay rate.
items.author: Dmitrij \.Zatuchin
items.summary: A pre-registered replication testing whether brand-mention rates in answers from the existing Gemini-3.1-Pro model remain stable enough over roughly 20 days to support act-on-able measurements. Using 162 requests across three languages with frozen decision rules registered on OSF, the study quantifies temporal drift in brand mention statistics.
items.reasoning: Methodologically rigorous pre-registration is commendable and relevant to the emerging field of LLM observability/brand measurement, but the scope is narrow, uses a single existing model, and the application domain is niche.

items.title: Improving Category-Aware Active Domain Adaptation via Uncertainty-Guided Region Coverage
items.content: arXiv:2610.19803v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Active domain adaptation researches focus on alleviating the annotation cost, which comprises source data and target data labelling, as well as enhancing the performance of unsupervised domain adaptation. However, optimizing the adaptation model based on the average accuracy can lead to the drop in performance of some difficult categories. To overcome this issue, a point-wise selection strategy built upon the influence function can be used to improve domain adaptation performance. In our work, we first address the sensitive and redundant aspects of point-wise selection, which can lead to overfitting of the acquisition function. We thus introduce a region-based approach that ensures the improvement of the adaptation model by maximizing a positive manifold coverage. An uncertainty score is further introduced to the selection mechanism to learn a better decision boundary for the target domain. In comprehensive experiments, our proposed method surpasses the first category-aware active domain adaptation baseline as well as existing active domain adaptation methods across multiple domain adaptation benchmarks. Our implementation is available at: https://github.com/nhtm2702/WHO IS NEXT.
items.author: My Tra Nguyen Huynh, Viet Cuong Ta
items.summary: This work improves active domain adaptation by replacing sensitive, redundancy-prone point-wise sample selection with a region-based approach that maximizes positive coverage under uncertainty, aiming to protect performance on difficult categories rather than only average accuracy. It builds on influence-function-based selection within category-aware ADA.
items.reasoning: A reasonable incremental improvement to active domain adaptation addressing overfitting of acquisition functions and per-category performance. The problem is real, but the techniques (uncertainty, region coverage, influence functions) are established combinations without clear novelty.

items.title: Event Cameras versus Frame Cameras for Synthetic-Aperture Imaging: A Simulation Study
items.content: arXiv:2610.20309v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Synthetic-aperture imaging (SAI) removes occluders such as foliage by integrating many views of a scene along a camera path. It has so far been used mainly with frame cameras. We ask whether an event camera has advantages for SAI, and answer the question in simulation, where both sensors see exactly the same scene and the same camera movement. A densely rendered Blender sequence is turned into frames with an EMVA~1288 noise model of an industrial global-shutter camera, and into an event stream with the v2e simulator parameterized like a Sony IMX636. The frames are integrated with the existing airborne optical sectioning renderer. For the events we add a new integration path that projects every single event onto the focal plane at its own interpolated pose, so no events have to be binned into frames. We compare the two sensors in three main runs and an additional dark high-speed test. In a bright scene at 25,m/s the frame camera records only three images on the path and cannot remove the occluder, while the event camera reconstructs the target, even after an event-rate controller drops most of its events to fit the camera link. At the same speed in a 5,lux scene the event camera no longer resolves the target either. In a 5,lux scene at 5,m/s both sensors reconstruct the target at similar quality. We also compare the data one traversal of the aperture costs. At high speed the capped event stream still shows the target at the same data volume as the three frames. At 1,m/s we compare both cameras at two matched data budgets, and there the event camera has no advantage over the frame camera in reconstruction quality. The data rate of the event camera depends on the scene and is highest exactly in the fast bright scenes where it is needed most.
items.author: Jakob Hinterholzer, Mohamed Youssef, Oliver Bimber
items.summary: This simulation study compares event cameras and frame cameras for synthetic-aperture occluder removal, using matched scene content and camera motion via a Blender rendering with realistic sensor noise models (EMVA 1288 for frames, v2e for a Sony IMX636-like event stream). The authors add a new per-event integration path projecting each event to the focal plane at its own timestamp.
items.reasoning: A careful, rigorous sensor-comparison methodology with a useful new event integration technique, but it is a simulation-only study answering a fairly narrow question; findings will need real-world confirmation before broad influence.

items.title: A Master-to-Simulation Interface with Demonstration-Trajectory Guidance for Vascular Intervention
items.content: arXiv:2610.19395v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Robotic vascular intervention can reduce radiation exposure to physicians and improve manipulation stability, but effective guidance remains challenging because conventional fluoroscopic images provide limited spatial information. This paper developed a vascular intervention interactive system that connects a real robotic master controller with the SOFA(Simulation Open Framework Architecture) physical simulation platform and reused successful operation trajectories as visual guidance in physical phantom experiments. Experiments were conducted to validate the master-to-SOFA control loop and to compare three guidance conditions: no guidance, centerline guidance, and successful-trajectory guidance. The control validation results showed reliable command delivery under velocity-mode operation. In the physical phantom experiment, centerline guidance showed no obvious improvement over no guidance. In contrast, successful trajectory guidance provided a clear performance benefit. Compared with the no-guidance condition, it reduced task completion time, collision number, rollback number, and rotation number by approximately 66.8%, 34.3%, 55.6%, and 66.7%, respectively. These results indicate that successful trajectories obtained under instrument-vessel interaction can provide practical guidance cues, offering a simple and effective visual assistance strategy for robotic vascular intervention experiments.
items.author: Mingyu Zou, Shuxiang Guo, Sheng Cao, Pengcheng Li, Jian Guo, Bin Wang, Mingchao Din

Phantom experiments compare no guidance, centerline guidance, and trajectory guidance conditions. It is a useful systems contribution for safer, lower-radiation endovascular procedures.

This paper developed a vascular intervention interactive system that connects a real robotic master controller with the SOFA(Simulation Open Framework Architecture) physical simulation platform and reused successful operation trajectories as visual guidance in physical phantom experiments. Experiments were conducted to validate the master-to-SOFA control loop and to compare three guidance conditions: no guidance, centerline guidance, and successful-trajectory guidance. The control validation results showed reliable command delivery under velocity-mode operation. In the physical phantom experiment, centerline guidance showed no obvious improvement over no guidance. In contrast, successful trajectory guidance provided a clear performance benefit. Compared with the no-guidance condition, it reduced task completion time, collision number, rollback number, and rotation number by approximately 66.8%, 34.3%, 55.6%, and 66.7%, respectively. These results indicate that successful trajectories obtained under instrument-vessel interaction can provide practical guidance cues, offering a simple and effective visual assistance strategy for robotic vascular intervention experiments.

items.title: Smart Fusion for Adaptive Visual-IMU Weighting in cuVSLAM Sparse Bundle Adjustment
items.content: arXiv:2610.20226v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In cuVSLAM, visual and inertial measurement unit (IMU) residuals are fused in sparse bundle adjustment (SBA) with a weighting fixed by pre-calibrated noise covariances, leaving no mechanism to adapt the visual-inertial balance at runtime. We introduce a scalar $\alpha\geq1$ that upscales the visual information matrix relative to the IMU preintegration constraint. Across the candidate set $\{1.0,2.0,5.0,10.0,20.0\}$, the resulting trajectories form two empirical performance regimes. The IMU-TRUST regime contains $\alpha\in\{1,2\}$ near the calibrated baseline, while the VISION-TRUST regime contains $\alpha\in\{10,20\}$. The intermediate value $\alpha=5$ is treated as a transition case. Differences within each regime are small relative to those observed between the regimes. This structure motivates reducing $\alpha$-selection to a binary decision. We train a lightweight Visual Quality Estimator (VQE), implemented as a multilayer perceptron with 914 trainable parameters. It maps a 10-dimensional visual quality feature vector assembled from statistics already maintained by the tracker to a per-SBA regime prediction. The proposed method reduces mean RMSE APE by $27.7\%$ and by $14.9\%$ under leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) on EuRoC MAV and TUM-VI Room, respectively.

items.title: Hierarchical Gaussian Processes for Survey Weighting: Local Equivalent Weights in Structured Populations
items.content: arXiv:2610.20321v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Regression-based survey weighting connects model-based population estimation with design-based inference through equivalent weights. For nonlinear models, equivalent weights can be defined locally through the sensitivity of a poststratified population estimator. However, conventional regression models may inadequately capture nonlinear relationships and complex interactions across sparse poststratification cells. We develop a survey-weighting framework based on hierarchical Gaussian process (HGP) regression, combining structured group-level effects with kernel-based smoothing to share information across related cells. We derive Gaussian posterior prediction formulas that exploit the structured covariance representation to reduce computational costs. We also establish a uniform convergence result for the posterior predictive mean under stated regularity conditions and construct local equivalent weights by matching the first-order sensitivity of a plug-in poststratified estimand to that of a weighted average of fitted response means, with both derivatives taken with respect to the latent mean-scale vector. Simulations show that HGP achieves lower population-weighted prediction error under nonparametric structure, whereas logistic regression performs well under correct parametric specification. Additional analyses examine sample size, frame coverage, subgroup prediction, and population-mean agreement. An application to the Future of Families and Child Wellbeing Study illustrates the method. Overall, this work extends local equivalent-weight construction to nonparametric modeling and provides a computational framework and conditional theoretical results for survey weighting in structured, sparse populations.

items.title: PPA 8: The Fermi Paradox, Fine-Tuning, and the SSA
items.content:
[This is the eighth piece in my series on the Parametric Process Assumption (PPA), a new model of anthropics. You should start here if you are just seeing this for the first time.

The previous piece is "Temporal Consistency and Texas Sharpshooting."

TLDR:

- The Fermi Paradox is easily resolved by realizing the universe is gigantic. This means that there are a huge number of possible worlds where life is very very far apart, despite the fact that it also abundant throughout the universe.
- If all you know is that you exist and that the universe is big and random, then the SSA, contrary to popular belief, is sufficient to conclude that life in the universe is abundant. The SIA, on the other hand, adds an additional bias on top.

The next piece is "Putting it all Together."]

### Big and Sparse

I confess that I’ve never really understood the Fermi Paradox. Or at least, I never understood why everyone always seemed so surprised by it.

If you haven’t heard, the Fermi Paradox is the apparent contradiction that, due to the vast age of the universe and the (seemingly) high probability of alien life, we should be observing signs of intelligent alien life all around the universe, and yet we don’t. If near-lightspeed travel were possible, for instance, it would presumably only take an intelligent species a few million years to colonize the entire Milky Way. For a galaxy that’s been around more than 13 billion years, the argument goes, you’d think someone would have gotten to that by now, right?...
items.author: Onid
items.summary: This eighth PPA piece argues that the Fermi Paradox dissolves once the sheer size of the universe is taken seriously, and claims the SSA alone (contrary to common belief) suffices to infer abundant life, with the SIA adding only extra bias. It connects anthropic selection effects to fine-tuning arguments.
items.reasoning: Original and clearly argued philosophical analysis of a well-known puzzle, but it is a mid-series installment on a niche topic outside core AI research, with limited empirical grounding.

items.title: Toward System One Clinical Intelligence: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning and Counterfactual Explainability of Decision Foundation Models
items.content: arXiv:2610.15029v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Automated disease classification from patient-reported symptoms requires balancing the speed of lightweight discriminative models against the contextual understanding and latency costs of autoregressive large language models (LLMs). Decision foundation models offer an alternative by mapping representations directly to candidate classes without free-form text generation. We adapt Clef-Flash, a 9-billion-parameter decision model built on a Qwen3.5 backbone, for 24-class disease classification on the Symptom2Disease benchmark. Using 4-bit quantized low-rank adaptation (QLoRA) with differential learning rates and a stratified split of 960 training and 240 test cases, the model achieves 95.42% diagnostic accuracy and a macro F1 score of 0.9551. This improves upon the reported zero-shot baselines of 61.67% for a remote API and 65.00% for a local unadapted initialization, and outperforms the ClinicalBERT baseline (90.90%). By evaluating candidate logits in a single forward pass without autoregressive decoding, inference takes under 80 milliseconds per record on a single GPU, yielding a reported 31-fold speedup over generative LLM baselines. To examine symptom-level evidence, we introduce a Leave-One-Symptom-Out (LOSO) counterfactual perturbation framework. Removing disease-defining symptom clauses in a psoriasis example reduces predicted-class confidence from 100.00% to 0.12% and shifts the prediction to impetigo with 99.59% confidence, while removing secondary systemic symptoms produces less than 0.01% change in confidence. These findings suggest that decision-based architectures can combine the linguistic capabilities of large foundation models with low-latency inference and symptom-level interpretability for clinical triage.

It also explores counterfactual explainability for the resulting classifier.

items.title: Bridging the Topological Divide: Dual-Branch Graph Distillation with Semantic Priors for Robust Cold-Start Recommendation
items.content: arXiv:2610.19578v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Graph Collaborative Filtering models have achieved remarkable success in recommendation systems. However, they inherently suffer from a catastrophic representation collapse in strict cold-start scenarios due to the topological isolation of unobserved items. While integrating multi-modal semantic features offers a potential remedy, directly mapping isolated semantic attributes into a globally topology-driven collaborative space frequently precipitates representation degradation and optimization conflicts. To bridge this fundamental structural divide, we propose DualGCN, an innovative Dual-Branch Graph Knowledge Distillation Framework. Operating under a decoupled two-stage training paradigm, DualGCN first constructs a robust collaborative teacher network where item representations are anchored by a topology-smoothed semantic prior, effectively reshaping the latent manifold. Subsequently, a semantic student branch employs a residual mapping mechanism and a magnitude-agnostic cosine distillation objective to achieve high-fidelity cross-modal alignment without disrupting established collaborative signals. Furthermore, we introduce a dynamic norm reconstruction mechanism to rigorously calibrate the physical scales of novel and warm items during global retrieval. Extensive experiments across three real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate that DualGCN significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in strict cold-start scenarios while comprehensively preserving recommendation accuracy for highly active items.
items.author: Yuanfeng Qiu
items.summary: DualGCN is a dual-branch graph knowledge distillation framework for cold-start recommendation that decouples collaborative and semantic branches to avoid representation collapse and optimization conflicts when mapping multimodal semantic features into topology-driven collaborative spaces. A two-stage training paradigm first builds a robust collaborative teacher, then transfers knowledge to the cold-start branch. It targets the known weakness of graph collaborative filtering on unobserved items.
items.reasoning: Competitive recommender-systems architecture work addressing a genuine cold-start problem, but single-authored, incrementally styled, and far from frontier AI research directions.

items.title: Controlling the latency in temporal coded spiking models for neuromorphic datasets
items.content: arXiv:2610.19732v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Exploiting temporal information in datasets with high temporal dependencies (such as spoken keyword recognition) by spiking models is still an open problem. Promising frameworks include Time-To-First coding (TTFS) and the inclusion of synaptic delays into learning. In TTFS, neurons are forced to spike at most once, forcing the network to found its learning on the spiking times of neurons rather than their spiking rate. Some models use the TTFS framework to directly compute the spiking time of Integrate-and-Fire (IF) or Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neurons. However, most models built in the TTFS framework have not been tested against datasets containing temporal information. Little is known about the latency of these models on temporal datasets, where the latency is the time taken by the network to correctly classify a sample. In this work, we study the behaviour of Delay Neural Networks (DeNN) models, i.e. models that directly compute the spiking time of neurons by bypassing the membrane potential and thresholding mechanisms of spiking neurons. We show how to analytically control their latency, and empirically study the latency-accuracy tradeoff in a dynamic temporal dataset.
items.author: Alban Gattepaille (I3S), Alexandre Muzy (ILLS)
items.summary: The authors study time-to-first-spike (TTFS) coded spiking models, examining the under-explored latency behavior of such networks on datasets with strong temporal dependencies like spoken keyword recognition. The work analyzes how TTFS frameworks with synaptic delays perform and how their latency can be controlled on temporal data.
items.reasoning: A focused contribution addressing a real gap in evaluating TTFS spiking models on genuinely temporal benchmarks, useful for the neuromorphic community. The scope is narrow and the findings are incremental within a specialized subfield.

items.title: PPA 7: Temporal Consistency and Texas Sharpshooting
items.content:
[This is the seventh piece in my series on the Parametric Process Assumption (PPA), a new model of anthropics. You should start here if you are just seeing this for the first time.

The previous piece is "Indexical Models Don't Have Diversity Biases."

TLDR:

- SSA is not "temporally consistent" - learning your brith rank causes an indexical update which can, for instance, change the probabilities of a fair coin that has not yet been tossed
- In order to perform an indexical update - the kind which causes distortions in the SSA and removes presumptuousness from the SIA - you need to learn your rank relative to some absolute property defined for all observers. Simply using a metric like "closest to the sun" would not help because all observers using such a procedure (picking the nearest star) would always find themselves the closest An actual update would require something like "ranked distance from largest star in the universe" or "life-bearing universe in multiverse with Nth largest gravitational constant," information we could not possibly hope to acquire

The next piece is "The Fermi Paradox, Fine-Tuning, and the SSA."]

One well-established failure mode of the SSA is that it is not "temporally consistent." I believe Nick Bostrom first pointed this out and Joe Carlsmith has an excellent write up on it here. 

The simplest example of inconsistency in the SSA is the Late-Flip version of the Sleeping Beauty Problem where the coin is flipped only after Sleeping Beauty is woken on Monday. In this scenario, P(Heads | Monday) seems as if it must be 0.5, since the coin hasn’t even been flipped yet. The SSA, however, assigns 2/3 credence to P(Heads | Monday).

In that sense, what we mean when we say “temporal consistency” is that for some event X with fixed and known probability, like the flip of a known-fair coin, learning our identity should not alter our credence in X if our identity was set before X happened. But there are two catches to this:...

The author argues genuine indexical updates require ranking relative to absolute, practically unknowable properties.

items.title: Integrating AIRL-Based Reward Estimation into a Control Method Using Fuzzy Inference and Policy Gradient
items.content: arXiv:2610.14723v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A method integrating policy gradient with fuzzy inference has been proposed. This method, hereafter referred to as the base model, has high flexibility with respect to the configuration of fuzzy inference rules and fuzzy representation. It can also automatically adjust the rule weights and the membership functions in the antecedent and consequent parts using the same framework for learning. In methods that integrate reinforcement learning with fuzzy inference, however, the reward function must be designed in advance. It is therefore useful to add learning-based reward estimation to the base model. This paper proposes a fuzzy control method that integrates a reward estimation mechanism based on the adversarial inverse reinforcement learning (AIRL) framework into the base model. The generative adversarial nets (GAN) framework adopted in AIRL, however, tends to suffer from unstable learning. To address this, the proposed method treats the policy of the base model as the generator and also uses the set of membership functions in the policy as the cost function of the discriminator. This configuration allows the discriminator update for reward estimation and the generator update for policy estimation to be performed simultaneously on the parameters shared by both, without estimating a value function. In simulations of an illustrative vehicle speed control task, the proposed method acquired policies with high generalization performance through stable and efficient learning.
items.author: Seiji Ishihara
items.summary: This paper combines adversarial inverse reinforcement learning (AIRL) reward estimation with a fuzzy inference control method trained via policy gradient. By learning rewards from demonstrations instead of hand-designing them, the approach removes a key manual bottleneck in fuzzy reinforcement learning while retaining the flexibility of automatically adjusted rule weights and membership functions.
items.reasoning: A niche but sensible integration of established techniques (fuzzy control, policy gradients, AIRL). Single author, incremental combination of known methods; limited evidence in the abstract of large-scale evaluation or SOTA claims.

items.title: RIECNN: Real-Time Image Enhanced CNN for Traffic Sign Recognition
items.content: arXiv:2610.15127v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Traffic sign recognition plays a crucial role in the development of autonomous cars to reduce the accident rate and promote road safety. It has been a necessity to address traffic signs that are affected significantly by the environment as well as poor real-time performance for deep-learning state-of-the-art algorithms. In this paper, we introduce Real-Time Image Enhanced CNN ({\our}) for Traffic Sign Recognition. {\our} is a real-time, novel approach that tackles multiple, diverse traffic sign datasets, and out-performs the state-of-the-art architectures in terms of recognition rate and execution time. items.title: SafeDSE: Joint Exploration of Safety Architecture Patterns, Mapping, and Scheduling for Dataflow Applications With Safety Arguments (Extended Version)
items.content: arXiv:2610.16213v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Embedded platforms increasingly host safety-related streaming functions next to less critical ones. Whether a safety architecture pattern, such as a doer/checker pair, protects a function depends on the cores that run its components. Their schedule must meet the throughput requirement, and mixing safety integrity levels (SILs) on one core raises development cost. This report presents SafeDSE, a design space exploration framework for synchronous dataflow applications. One declarative constraint model decides the pattern of each actor, the placement that the fault model requires, the static-order schedule, and the platform, and prices SIL promotion. Guards activate the chosen patterns in a fixed graph that holds all of them, and node potentials encode throughput. An independent verifier re-checks every solution, and a generator turns its checks into evidence of a safety argument in Goal Structuring Notation. On 9 benchmark instances under period bounds, no rule that fixes patterns before mapping was both always feasible and never more expensive under conservative pricing, while joint exploration was. In the generated arguments, 49 to 62% of the leaves cite verifier checks; the rest are claims a mapping cannot discharge. Optimality within the model was proven for all synthetic graphs with up to 16 actors. This extended version adds the full model, the verifier and generator in detail, the complete catalog and parameters, and a proof of the potential characterization. It also reports every experiment per instance, a mutation analysis of the verifier, and the negative results of the development.

items.title: DWI Connectome-based Sex Classification in Young using Supervised Variational Autoencoder
items.content: arXiv:2610.16348v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: During adolescence, significant changes in brain development are influenced by hormonal changes that impact both the body and the brain. This study presents sex classification in 787 young adults having age range of 15-25 years using Diffusion-weighted (DWI) structural connectome, focusing on 82 Desikan-Killiany atlas ROIs. A supervised variational autoencoder (SVAE) is used to extract latent space features from DWI connectome data. Although several studies explored differences in brain structure and function between sexes, the main contribution of this study lies in incorporating SVAE to learn a compact, regularized latent representation for the task of sex classification. Initial exploratory data analysis shows that these features can capture the differences in sex-specific latent space patterns. Subsequently, the learned latent space SVAE features are fed to different ML models for sex classification. Among the considered ML classifiers, the multi-layer perceptron yields the highest accuracy of 80% in classifying sex. This demonstrates the effectiveness of SVAE in learning compact, informative representations from DWI connectome for sex classification. The present work highlights the potential of using DWI brain connectomics and deep learning to differentiate sex, paving the way for future research on diverse populations that may include transgender individuals, to better understand sex-related variations in brain structure.

items.title: From Conceptual EneMonIE to an Executable Backend: A Modular Architecture for Energy Information Extractionand Grounded Question Answering
items.content: arXiv:2610.17243v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The original EneMonIE proposal describes a Web-based semantic system for continuously monitoring energy trends through targeted information extraction from heterogeneous online media. This article presents EneMonIE-Backend, an implementation-derived redesign that converts that conceptual pipeline into a modular, executable, and application-independent backend. The architecture separates five concerns: data sources, acquisition and normalization, semantic processing, knowledge organization, and persistent storage. It operationalizes configurable connectors for RSS feeds, URL collections, arXiv, social-media JSON files, and open-data CSV files; it also introduces question-driven Web search and scraping. Relevant documents pass through energy categorization, named entity recognition, temporal and event extraction, source sensitive sentiment analysis, and extractive summarization. The resulting semantic representations support entity co-occurrence graphs, cross-document interlinking, cluster-level information fusion, and relational persistence in SQLite. Three grounded question-answering paths are exposed at the backend level: live Web evidence, the stored corpus, and selected configured resources. Answer generation uses a language model when configured and otherwise falls back to deterministic extractive output. Unlike the original proposal, the presented architecture deliberately excludes the user-interface and server-side application layers, allowing the semantic core to be embedded in different applications. A deterministic smoke validation confirms relevance filtering, persistence, clustering, evidence retrieval, and document deletion. The work provides a reproducible architectural basis for future evaluation on larger multilingual energy corpora.

items.title: Better Capturing Interactions Between Products in~Retail: Revisited Negative Sampling for~Basket Choice Modeling
items.content: arXiv:2610.17963v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Brick-and-mortar retailers face many different challenges that involve understanding thoroughly its products catalog and customer preferences. In particular, assortment optimization - proposing the ideal mix of products - and promotion planning hold a pivotal role in their strategy. By leveraging sales data, retailers can make informed decisions on which products to sell and how to manage inventory, based on customer preferences as well as regional and seasonal trends. It is especially crucial to capture interactions between products, in order to minimize the number of items that cannibalize each other's sales and to ensure that complementary products, which are often purchased together, are conjointly available and sold across all stores. In this paper, we propose a model of shopping basket that learns embeddings to represent interactions between products, prices and stores. Our model is built to uncover sales patterns from very large transaction datasets. In particular, the optimization loss is computed with random negative samples in order to overcome the computational bottlenecks that arise with large number of items. Our experiments on synthetic data show the efficiency of drawing such negative samples based on the actual assortment of available products, with better results than approaches from the literature. We also validate our approach by training and evaluating our model on a dataset composed of millions of transactions from Fortenova Group, one of the leading retail company in Southeast Europe. Our model showcases promising applications in the sector of retail, with enriched interfaces to efficiently support category managers.

items.summary: This arXiv paper addresses assortment optimization and promotion planning for brick-and-mortar retailers by improving basket choice modeling, which requires capturing interactions between products such as substitution (cannibalization) and complementarity. The authors propose a revisited negative sampling approach to better learn these product interactions from sales data. The work matters because accurate preference modeling directly informs which products retailers stock and how they plan promotions across stores.

However, it is a niche improvement to negative sampling in choice modeling rather than a fundamental advance, and it is not central to frontier AI research themes like large language models, alignment, or novel architectures. Novelty and broader impact appear limited to the retail operations domain.

items.title: How Reliable Are Large Language Models for Soil Organic Carbon Assessment? An Australian Benchmark
items.content: arXiv:2610.18201v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) is an indicator of agricultural soil condition and carbon storage, but numerical outputs from large language models (LLMs) require validation before use in monitoring or management. We evaluated seven general-purpose LLM configurations on three direct-response tasks: estimating 0--10 cm SOC concentrations for 308 Australian paddocks under two information conditions, calculating SOC stock in 120 matched scenarios, and comparing 300 paddock pairs. References were measured SOC records or deterministic calculations; response validity, repeated-call dispersion and estimated API cost were assessed separately. Additional measured soil attributes reduced concentration mean absolute error by 13--62\% across configurations, although high-SOC underprediction and paddock-specific errors persisted. Six configurations were highly accurate in stock calculations using equation-native units without coarse fragments, but accuracy declined with physically equivalent alternative units. Pairwise accuracy was 90.5--94.6\% overall and 59.1--70.9\% for 52 closely separated pairs; some configurations were sensitive to presentation order. Nearly all outputs were parseable, without necessarily being correct. The benchmark identifies three distinct requirements for AI-mediated SOC assessment: agreement with measured concentrations, unit-consistent stock calculations and reliable discrimination between sites. These findings support task-specific validation and auditable calculations, rather than unverified use of LLM outputs as ecological evidence.

items.title: APTree: Extended Behavior Trees for Adaptive and Scalable Automated Robotic Task Planning in Construction
items.content: arXiv:2610.18523v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Task planning for robots in off-site construction prefabrication is primarily manual, leading to planning inefficiencies and reluctance to adopt robotic solutions. Existing approaches provide limited support for scalable, modular automated task planning and localized runtime replanning. This paper proposes APTree, a model-driven framework that integrates automated task planning with modular task execution using behavior trees as the execution model. APTree repeatedly applies and coordinates heterogeneous symbolic planners to automatically generate and compose modular task plans at runtime. To support this approach, we develop a domain-specific language for the formal specification and validation of task plans, together with a compatible execution engine. We evaluate APTree on the real-world livMatS Biomimetic Shell pavilion, where it models the construction robotic fabrication domain, detects injected specification and planning errors at design time and runtime, and automatically generates large-scale task plans by coordinating three symbolic planners across numerous planning modules. A machine-checked formal analysis further shows that composed execution and local replanning are safe under explicitly stated assumptions, including planner soundness and non-interference of generated plans, providing practitioners with explicit conditions for dependable plan composition. APTree thus enables construction practitioners to leverage automated task planning without requiring detailed knowledge of symbolic planning techniques or APTree's internal implementation.

items.title: Sequential Learning-Based Physics-Informed Neural Network Modeling for Parameter Estimation on a Power Converter
items.content: arXiv:2610.20041v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A staged physics-informed neural network (PINN) is proposed for identifying the inductance, capacitance and parasitic resistances of a DC buck converter from time-domain data. Gradients are released in the order of L to C to rL to rC, a sequence derived from sensitivity analysis. The five-stage schedule recovers L and C to within 5% and the series ESR to 10%, while a three-stage variant attains the same accuracy 11% faster. An 84 factorial sweep confirms that the trained PINN remains accurate for simultaneous 8% perturbations of all four components, achieving a waveform RMSE of 2.6 x 10-2 over 5 ms-an order-of-magnitude better than a simultaneous-training baseline.

items.title: Learning to Select Features with Manifold Deep Unfolding PCA
items.content: arXiv:2610.19436v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Unsupervised feature selection (UFS) is of great significance in image processing and pattern recognition. Nevertheless, existing model-based methods often rely on manually tuned hyperparameters, while deep learning-based methods generally require massive training data. To address these issues, this paper proposes an efficient manifold deep unfolding feature selection network (MDUFS-Net). Technically, we first incorporate the $\ell_{2,0}$-norm into the classic principal component analysis (PCA) framework, then unfold the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)-based iterative algorithm into an end-to-end trainable network, thereby enabling automatic parameter learning. Moreover, a manifold optimization strategy is developed to improve the numerical robustness. On this basis, we further extend MDUFS-Net into an enhanced variant called MDUFS-Net+ by introducing the $\ell_{0}$-norm for more discriminative feature representations. Extensive experiments validate that our proposed MDUFS-Net and MDUFS-Net+ outperform state-of-the-art methods in the UFS task, with promising performance in clustering. Our code is available at https://github.com/xianchaoxiu/MDUFS.
